_comment: Slakh2100 train split, pre-encoded with the streamgen accompaniment control. Same mechanism as local_babyslakh_streamgen.json, on the full corpus with the official Slakh splits, which is what 1.2 needs to say anything about generalization. Pass --sample_size on the CLI, never as a key here: pre_encode_dataset.py's merge_config_into_args treats any argparse default that is not None as CLI-supplied, so a 'sample_size' key would be silently ignored. As run on 2026-09-08 the sbatch scripts pass --sample_size 587853 --pad --batch_size 8, i.e. a 13.3s / 144-frame window taken from the START of every track (the pre-encode path sets random_crop=False). The alternative, if whole tracks are wanted, is --sample_size 16760832 (4092 frames, 380s, the 95th percentile track length) with --batch_size 1 and no --pad; note that the silence-fraction cutoff below means something quite different at that length. Augmentation: 'augment_variants' writes that many copies of the split, variant 0 unaugmented and the rest each rolling a time-stretch rate from 'augment_time_stretch' and a pitch shift from +/- 'augment_pitch_semitones'. Both the stretch and the pitch shift go to the drums and the accompaniment with the same values ('augment_pitch_scope': 'all'), so a variant is the whole arrangement in a new key at a new tempo; the shared rate is what keeps the two frame-aligned. Set 'augment_pitch_scope' to 'controls' to hold the drums at their original tuning while still re-keying the accompaniment. Each variant is a fresh pass, so the stochastic stem submix is re-rolled per variant too. Encode time and disk scale with the variant count. Sanity check: 'sanity_check_samples' is counted PER VARIANT and the dataloader is unshuffled, so 2 x 'augment_variants' items are decoded back to audio into <output_path>/_sanity_check — the same tracks in every variant, so the variants are A/B-able against each other. Build the page with scripts/make_listening_page.py; each variant gets its own card stating the rate and interval it was written with. Silence filtering: items whose target or accompaniment is silent over the encoded window are DROPPED, not replaced (they leave a gap in the latent ids). The default is an RMS floor of -50 dBFS; '--max_silence_fraction' adds a percentage-of-silence limit and is off by default. THE CHOSEN CUTOFF FOR SLAKH AT THIS WINDOW IS 0.85, decided 2026-09-09 by decoding two items from each 0.1-wide silence band (scripts/sample_silence_buckets.py) and listening. The first encode used 0.3, taken from 17 BabySlakh tracks, which on Slakh sat below the corpus target median (0.346) and on the mode of its distribution and kept only 56 of 270 validation items; at 0.85 the limit is a backstop against near-empty windows -- the RMS floor's blind spot, since 99.9% silence with one full-scale hit measures about -31 dBFS -- and keeps ~784 of 1289 train items. It must be passed on the CLI and the sbatch scripts currently pass NO fraction limit, so check the sbatch before relying on one, and set the same value for both splits or they are not comparable. Every sidecar JSON carries a 'levels' block (rms_dbfs, silence_fraction per stream) so a cutoff can be read off a first pass, and '_skipped.json' records what went and why. Note that the 'levels' block is only written for items that SURVIVE the filter, so a filtered pass gives a distribution truncated at its own thresholds and cannot be used to choose them -- read a cutoff off an RMS-only or '--no_silence_filter' pass with scripts/analyze_silence_levels.py. Inventory of which root holds which filter: docs/data/slakh-streamgen.md. See experiments/01-streamgen-conditioning/04-silence-filtering.md.
